intervals.quote: The winning entry was the sodium iodide and lead-glass array proposed by the group from Columbia and Stony Brook with Leon Lederman as spokesman.

physics_goals.quote: had photon energy resolution clearly superior to that of the CLEO-1 detector, and was ideally suited for the study of radiative transitions among the upsilon bound states
physics_goals.value: Upsilon spectroscopy: photon energy measurements for radiative transitions among the upsilon bound states

summary.plain: A compact detector made of sodium iodide and lead-glass crystals at the north interaction point of Cornell's CESR ring, built by Columbia and Stony Brook universities. Its photon energy resolution made it ideal for the transitions between bottom-quark Upsilon states, which it studied from 1979 to about 1990.
summary.technical: CUSB (Columbia University-Stony Brook): non-magnetic NaI and lead-glass shower detector at CESR's north interaction region, led by L. Lederman then P. and J. Franzini; upgraded to CUSB-II with BGO crystals (PAC decision January 1984; NIM A263 (1988) 35); radiative transitions to χb states, first indication of the B*; terminated about 1990 after one more Υ(4S) run.
